draft.title: Predicting precipitation
card: The ion product, Q, is worked out like Ksp, but with the ion concentrations at the moment of mixing. These need not be equilibrium values.
If Q is greater than Ksp, the solution holds more ions than it can at equilibrium. A precipitate forms until the concentrations fall to the Ksp value.
If Q is less than or equal to Ksp, no precipitate forms. The solution is unsaturated, or just saturated.
When two solutions are mixed, the volume increases. Find each ion's new concentration after dilution before calculating Q.
draft.remember: Precipitate forms when Q is greater than Ksp. Dilute the ions first when mixing.

a.q: A mixture of two solutions has a Q for barium sulfate of 5 × 10-9. The Ksp is 1 × 10-10. What happens?
opts: The Ksp rises to match Q
a.why: Q is greater than Ksp, so the mixture holds more ions than it can at equilibrium and solid forms. It is not unsaturated, and Ksp stays the same at a given temperature.

b.q: 50 mL of 0.020 M Ca2+ is mixed with 50 mL of 0.020 M SO4 2-. Ksp of CaSO4 is 5 × 10-5. What happens?
opts: No precipitate, as Q is 1 × 10-4 only after... see below
b.why: Mixing doubles the volume, so each ion falls to 0.010 M. Q = 0.010 × 0.010 = 1.0 × 10-4, which is greater than 5 × 10-5, so a precipitate forms. Using 0.020 M each gives 4.0 × 10-4 because the dilution is ignored.
b.clue: Each volume is doubled, so halve each concentration.

proposal.title: Predicting precipitation
card: The ion product, Q, is worked out like Ksp, but with the ion concentrations at the moment of mixing. These need not be equilibrium values.
If Q is greater than Ksp, the solution holds more ions than it can at equilibrium. Solid precipitates until Q falls to equal Ksp. Ksp itself stays the same at a given temperature.
If Q is less than Ksp, no precipitate forms and the solution is unsaturated. If Q equals Ksp, the solution is just saturated.
When two solutions are mixed, the total volume grows, so each ion is diluted. Find each ion's new concentration before calculating Q.
proposal.remember: Precipitate forms when Q is greater than Ksp. Dilute the ions first when mixing.

b.q: 50 mL of 0.020 M Ca²⁺ is mixed with 50 mL of 0.020 M SO₄²⁻. Ksp of CaSO₄ is 5 × 10⁻⁵. What happens?

b.clue: The total volume is double each starting volume.
